objectives: Hear /k/ followed immediately by /r/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend /k/ and /r/ smoothly without adding a vowel between them.
Distinguish the initial cr blend from /k/ alone and from other taught blends.
Say the complete word after blending the onset with the rest of its sounds.
concepts: The initial cr blend contains /k/ followed by /r/.
Both consonant sounds remain audible in the blend.
No extra vowel is inserted between /k/ and /r/.
Listening for the complete word helps confirm the blend.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Crab starts with /k/ followed by /r/; cap starts with /k/ alone.
Keep /k/ and /r/ together, then blend the short /i/ and final /b/.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel and saying kuh-rab instead of blending smoothly.
Leaving out /r/ and saying cab for crab.
Guessing before hearing the complete word.
keyTakeaways: Do not add a vowel between the consonants.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
Check that the complete word matches the sounds.
revisionPoints: Crab and crib both begin with cr.
Do not insert a vowel between /k/ and /r/.
Listen to the whole word before choosing.
